name: Beach stones: size follows the waves
plain: Where stones collect on a gentle shore, exposed beaches (lots of open water to windward) get big, round, well-sorted boulders with a storm berm at the top; sheltered coves get small, mixed cobble over mud.
confidence: medium: curves from World's levels/downeast/coast_rules.json (21 Oct), checked against the Bar Harbor shore and cited above; Matt's field corrections still to come

sources.cite: Bird, E.C.F. (2008) Coastal Geomorphology: An Introduction, 2nd ed. Wiley.
sources.note: shingle and boulder beaches coarsen, sort and round with wave energy; a storm berm at the top of exposed ones

sources.cite: Kelley, J.T. et al. (1989) The Maine coastal zone: an atlas (Maine Geological Survey)
sources.note: Maine pocket beaches: boulder and cobble on exposed headlands, cobble over mud in sheltered coves
the rule's purpose, in his words

where_note: habitat 13/21 (developed) counts on the shore: the 30 m land cover runs over the beaches in town (the beach below Agamont Park is 'developed, dense'); the height curve keeps the rule on the shore
